tool: Antigravity CLI (agy) 1.5.15 in print mode, run in an empty directory outside the repository: `agy -p "<request>" --model gemini-4-neon-high --mode accept-edits --sandbox --output-format json`. The agent hands the request to its built-in image-generator subagent, which writes the image prompt and calls its generate_image tool.
model: gemini-3.1-flash-image behind generate_image (the service named it in a capacity error of the same session; the tool does not report it on success); agent gemini-4-neon-high; image-generator subagent gemini-4-hydrogen-tiered-high.
prompt: Seamless tileable PBR diffuse albedo surface texture of a black industrial rubber conveyor belt top cover. Fine, uniform, matte rough vulcanized rubber grain across the entire square frame, very dark charcoal black tones with subtle light micro-scuffs, faint realistic wear, and minimal fine dust embedded in the pores. Viewed perfectly straight-on from an orthographic top-down angle, completely flat and even shadowless diffuse lighting from all directions, zero shadows, zero specular highlights or glare, zero vignetting or brightness gradients across edges, no perspective distortion, uniform edge-to-edge density and scale so opposite edges wrap and tile seamlessly in a 3D material. Strictly pure continuous rubber surface only: no belt edges, no seams, no objects, no text, no logos, no markings. Photorealistic macro material scan aesthetic.
request: Generate exactly one image with aspect ratio 1:1 and nothing else. Image description: A seamless tileable surface texture of a black rubber conveyor belt top cover: a fine, uniform, matte rough rubber grain with subtle light wear and faint dust, very dark charcoal tones, viewed perfectly straight on (orthographic, top-down), completely flat even diffuse lighting, no shadows, no specular highlights, no vignetting, no perspective, no objects, no text, no logos, no markings, uniform detail across the whole frame so it can tile seamlessly in a 3D material, photorealistic, square.
postProcessing: 1. ImageMagick 7.1.2-36, a one-off conversion of the generated JPEG to an 8-bit RGB PNG: `magick source.jpg -strip -colorspace sRGB -type TrueColor PNG24:source.png`. 2. `bun tools/plant/textures.ts prepare rubber-belt source.png`: the last 128 columns and rows are cross-faded into the first ones (seamless, 896x896), the broad light and shade is removed (a wrapping box blur of radius 112 subtracted, the mean kept), and the image is area-averaged to 512x512. 3. `bun tools/plant/textures.ts derive` writes normal.png, roughness.png and metalness.png from basecolor.png.
